thread_analysis.thread_summary: Internal Allion Japan lab-troubleshooting thread (Itsuo Sakai, Kousuke Nakayama) for Toytec's RF PHY test, dated October 2024. This thread substantially overlaps with thread_0028 (the broader customer-facing Toytec engagement), documenting the same underlying RF PHY DTM command-response troubleshooting incident -- COM port assignment errors, confusion between the customer's 'preparation' vs. 'test operation method' document sections, and an interfering FCC_assist tool -- from a more internal, lab-engineer-focused angle. Refer to thread_0028's case files for the customer-facing narrative and final root-cause resolution (the FCC_assist1.0.4.exe tool conflicting with the COM port InterLab needed).
all_questions_found: What does an 'Unable to open COM8' error during DTM pre-test setup indicate, and is SkipCommand a valid workaround? (see thread_0027_case_01)

(Duplicated in thread_0028) The customer's sample document contains a 'test operation method' section meant for radio-law/FCC testing, not SIG DTM testing -- see thread_0028's case files for the fuller resolution, including the FCC_assist1.0.4.exe tool conflict that was the ultimate root cause.
(Administrative, not separately cased) Test Plan file delivery to the lab -- routine project administration.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread's standalone contribution (case_01) is the specific 'Unable to open COM8' diagnostic detail and the explicit caution against using SkipCommand as an invalid workaround. The fuller technical resolution of this same incident (the FCC_assist1.0.4.exe tool occupying the COM port InterLab needed) is documented in thread_0028.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0027_case_01 and thread_0028's case files for the fuller picture.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: See thread_0028's analysis for the fuller account of the root-cause discovery process and the lab's own acknowledged initial mistake.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: This thread is a partial, more-internal capture of the same incident documented more completely in thread_0028 -- when two thread captures cover the same underlying incident, treat the more complete one as authoritative and cross-reference rather than duplicating case content.
